title: Optimal Median Selection Networks (n = 7..16): minimize comparator count
description: Pure Lean 4.36.0 (zero Mathlib) certified optimization of size-minimal comparator median selection networks on n = 7..16 wires, with Knuth's Zero-One Principle for order statistics and an O(n^2) bit-sliced 2^n-input threshold-DP kernel evaluator formally proved inside `SelectNet/Spec.lean`. Ten independent hill-climb tracks start from textbook Batcher odd-even merge-exchange seeds (16..63) and target SorterHunter's best known records (13..46, open frontiers for n ≥ 12), pinned to `bertdobbelaere/SorterHunter@3d8b345` (MIT).

tasks.title: Minimize 7-wire median selection network size (baseline 16)
tasks.description: Submit a comparator network on 7 wires in `SelectNet/Net7.lean` (`SelectNet.score7` and `SelectNet.net7`) selecting wire 3 (exact median). Seeded with textbook Batcher odd-even merge-exchange sort (16 comparators; Proven optimal (13)). Frozen `SelectNet/Bound7.lean` kernel-verifies well-formedness (`i < j < 7`), comparator count, and exact median selection on all 2^7 Boolean inputs via `decide +kernel`, lifting to every linear order by the formalized Zero-One Principle in `SelectNet/Spec.lean`.
